html:
A war between the Eastern Roman and Sasanian empires from 541 to 562 for control of Lazica, a kingdom on the eastern Black Sea coast in what is now western Georgia, the ancient Colchis.

Lazica was a Roman client. In 541 its king, Gubazes II, angry at Roman officials who had seized control of trade, called in the Persian shah Khosrow I. Persian troops took the fortress of Petra on the coast. For Persia, Lazica meant a port on the Black Sea; for Rome, a Persian fleet there would threaten Constantinople. The Lazi soon found Persian rule worse and turned back to Rome.

The war dragged on in mountains and river valleys, with sieges and ambushes, while Justinian was also fighting in Italy and the plague struck both empires. Gubazes was murdered by Roman generals in 555. A truce in 557 led to the Fifty-Year Peace Treaty of 562, under which Persia left Lazica and Rome paid a yearly sum of gold.
sum: A war between the Eastern Roman and Sasanian empires from 541 to 562 for control of Lazica, a kingdom on the eastern Black Sea coast in what is now western Georgia, the ancient Colchis.
